subject: Split-pay options for Sovereign Audit Logs & HSM — concession framing
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@composurehealth.com>, Daniel Ortiz <daniel.ortiz@composurehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Split-pay options for Sovereign Audit Logs & HSM — concession framing

Hi Maya / Daniel —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, you asked us to lay out a path that keeps Composure’s residency preference (US-only logs + on-demand HSM seats) while limiting near-term recurring spend. Two pragmatic packaging options attached in the pricing summary (pricing_summary_v3.xlsx). High level: 

Option A — Hosted HIPAA + Add-ons (fastest, lowest operational lift)
- Hosted HIPAA baseline (model inference hosted in Redwood with HIPAA attestation)
- Audit logs: managed audit log retention (30/90/365 tiers) as a recurring line item
- KMS/HSM: managed key service + optional HSM seats (per-seat per-month)
- Implementation credit: one-time onboarding credit to offset initial evidence & attestation work

Option B — Hybrid Residency (data anchored in Composure VPC / regional residency)
- Residency seat (one-time activation + monthly capex-equivalent or amortized credit)
- Audit logs: per-ingest or per-gb recurring (can be structured as consumption to keep base fees lower)
- HSM: on-prem proxy or dedicated HSM seats with reduced per-seat rate if part of residency commit

What I want to surface for your procurement team: we can do a split-pay / amortization construct so the heavy implementation cost is recognized up front but invoiced as credits over N months to match your budgeting preference. Example in the spreadsheet shows 12-18 month amortization paths.

Questions for you:
1) Would procurement prefer an amortized credit schedule (we show 12 vs 18 months in the sheet) or a capped one-time activation fee?
2) Any hard constraints on capital vs recurring splits?
3) Timeline for evidence delivery you need to close (SOC2 attestation, KMS architecture diagram, HSM vendor certs)?

If you’re open, Ben can sketch a quick commercial counter-proposal with numbers that mirror the approach you like.

Attachment: pricing_summary_v3.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Thanks,
Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Maya Singh <maya@composurehealth.com>

Cc: Daniel Ortiz <daniel.ortiz@composurehealth.com>
Date: 2028-07-01T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Split-pay options for Sovereign Audit Logs & HSM — concession framing

Thanks Kim —

This is helpful. A few notes from procurement and finance:
- Our finance team is pushing for a capex-forward approach for the residency activation. They prefer a one-time activation fee capitalized to the project rather than a recurring uplift.
- If Redwood can amortize the implementation/attestation support across 18 months and keep the recurring HSM seats below $X/month for the first year, that would be much easier to get internal sign-off.
- We also need a clear evidence delivery timeline — SOC2 bridging letter, KMS key custody diagram, and HSM vendor whitepaper by the time we execute PO. Can you confirm delivery dates for those?

I’ve looped Daniel (budget owner) on this thread to keep him in the procurement loop — he’ll weigh in on pricing tolerance.

Best,
Maya
Maya Singh
Head of Procurement, Composure Health
maya@composurehealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-01T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Split-pay options for Sovereign Audit Logs & HSM — concession framing

Kim / team —

Thanks — posting a quick commercial alternative to present to Maya/Daniel that addresses the capex ask while protecting Redwood economics: 

Commercial sketch (illustrative):
- Residency activation: one-time $75,000 activation fee (we can invoice as capex)
- Implementation/attestation credit: $60,000 credit applied to first 18 months of recurring (i.e., $3,333/mo credit) — effectively amortizes our onboarding work but reduces the first-year cash burden for Composure
- HSM seats: normal list $2,000/seat/mo — offer a promotional 25% discount on first 6 months if they commit to residency seat for 12 months
- Audit logs: tiered per-gb tiers; propose a 6-month consumption cap for predictable spend
\Notes / tradeoffs:
- The $60k credit is above our standard but reasonable given expected TCV. We’ll need LA approval to go deeper.
- Require a 12-month minimum residency commit (to protect seat discounts).
\If procurement is firm on AMORTIZE vs CAPEX, we can flip the numbers (e.g., invoice residency as one-time and amortize the credit as a separate line). Recommend we propose the above as a preferred path and offer an 18-month amortization as a concession.

I can size the exact math and produce a redline for their PO if Kim wants — ping me and I’ll run numbers.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Growth Rep, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Forwarding the thread. Procurement pushed for capex treatment; Ben sketched a path that amortizes our onboarding credit while putting residency as a one-time activation fee. My recommendation: we approve up to $60k of implementation credit amortized over 18 months, and a limited promotional discount on HSM seats (20% off first 9 months) if they sign a 12-month residency commit. This preserves ARR while giving procurement the capex-friendly invoicing they want.

Kim / Ben —

I’m comfortable approving a modified concession to keep the deal moving. Approve the following with conditions: 

Approved commercial items:
- Residency activation invoiced as a one-time fee and capitalized on Composure side: capex invoice for $75k.
- Implementation/attestation credit capped at $60k, amortized over 18 months (apply as monthly credits to reduce recurring for year one and two).
- HSM seat discount: 15% off standard list for the first 9 months (not cumulative with other promos).

Conditions & guardrails:
1) Require an SLA appendix and rollback policy (automatic fallback to Hosted HIPAA variant) in the SOW.
2) Lock-in: 12-month minimum residency commitment to get the discounts and credit.
3) Evidence delivery: SOC2 bridging letter, KMS custody diagram, and HSM vendor certs must be delivered within 30 days of SOW execution.
4) No additional ad-hoc concessions without explicit sign-off from Sales Ops.

Next steps: Kim — send the updated SOW with the above terms and include the SOW and pricing workbook in the DocuSign envelope. I’ll sign if the SOW contains the SLA appendix and rollback clause.

Attachment: SOW_CH-4921_v1.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)
